clue.text: Whimsical tale of hairy adventures?

parts.note: a long rambling joke with a pointless ending is named after a tale about an unkempt hound, so a story of 'hairy' doings fits it literally

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fanciful yarn full of hair-raising exploits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' suggests danger, but read it literally: the tale is about a dog with a shaggy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a long-winded joke or anecdote whose payoff is deliberately pointless, a classic whimsical yarn.

clue.text: Leave a prohibition on academic

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' places the ban piece above the academic piece

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban
a don is a university lecturer, an academic

explanation.surface: Someone is told to quit because of a ban imposed on a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something behind for good is to desert or forsake it.

clue.text: Left Gateshead at one

parts.note: split as 'Gate's head', the head (first letter) of gate is G
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone departed from Gateshead, a town in north-east England, at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town near Newcastle in north-east England; split it as 'Gate's head' to get the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has left has departed and is no longer here.

clue.text: Relaid again old path across square

indicators.note: relaid means laid down again in a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the next two words are reordered

explanation.surface: An old garden path across a town square is being relaid once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanting line from one corner of a square to the opposite corner crosses it obliquely.

clue.text: Start to gain admission to the upper classes

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here the first letter of gain

parts.note: admission to a place is entry into it

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to begin gaining access to high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed families just below the nobility form the well-born social class.

clue.text: Reprimand for marking as correct

definitions.meaning: putting a check mark against an item, accepting it as right or done

explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is a dressing-down, while putting check marks against items on a list is marking them as right.

clue.text: Aggressive behaviour of a politician in anger

indicators.note: the words 'a politician' are set within the word for anger

parts.note: rage is intense anger
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Someone describes the violent conduct of an MP who has lost their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent, uncontrolled rushing about is wild aggressive conduct.

clue.text: Fighter takes drinks of spirits in his underwear

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter in the ring
shorts are small measures of spirits such as whisky

explanation.surface: A boxer downs some whisky while still in his pants.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'short' is a small measure of spirits, as opposed to a long drink like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-fitting men's undershorts are a kind of male underwear.

clue.text: Support isn't commonly found in the sea

indicators.note: one word is found inside another, so the colloquial form is placed within

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
ain't is the common, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A claim that some kind of backing is not usually to be found at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To support something is to uphold it or keep it going.

clue.text: Appeared to have nothing but a small role

parts.note: came means arrived or appeared
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An actor showed up and was given nothing but a bit part.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief appearance by a well-known actor in a film or play is a small part.

clue.text: Unacknowledged author of some spirited book?

definitions.text: Unacknowledged author of some spirited book?

parts.words: Unacknowledged author of some spirited book?
parts.note: an uncredited writer who produces work for someone else, also humorously a phantom writing about spirits

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who secretly wrote a lively book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' suggests lively, but read it as haunted by spirits: the author is a spectre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired writer produces a book published under another person's name, so remains uncredited.

clue.text: Conceal animal skin

definitions.meaning: the pelt of a beast, often for leather

explanation.definitionFit: To keep something out of sight is to conceal it, and a beast's pelt used for leather is its skin.

clue.text: Wild action-redo to make harmonious

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the hyphenated phrase are scrambled

explanation.surface: A frantic re-take of a film scene is meant to bring things into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the ten letters of ACTION-REDO.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring parts into proper working relation is to make them work together smoothly.

clue.text: Priest's to encourage something only partly good

parts.note: a curate is an assistant priest; the possessive is kept
to egg someone on is to encourage them

explanation.surface: A clergyman is urged to do something only half-right.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from a Punch cartoon in which a timid curate, served a bad egg, says parts of it are excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a thing with good and bad parts mixed together.

clue.text: Peculiar individual case

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the form for one item rather than several

explanation.definitionFit: Something odd is strange or unusual, and in grammar the form for one item rather than several is the non-plural.

clue.text: Terrible woman removes pair leading advance

indicators.note: the leading pair of letters, the first two, are taken off the front of the word for advance

parts.note: progress is forward movement, an advance

explanation.surface: A dreadful woman blocks two people at the head of a forward march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removes pair leading' takes PR, the first two letters, off PROGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monster from folk tales, or a frightening woman, is a fearsome female figure.

clue.text: Ungenerous period for interval

parts.note: mean means stingy, ungenerous
a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: A stingy stretch of time is offered as a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The time between two events is the intervening period.

clue.text: Little Australian cut grass back to play innings

indicators.note: back says the word for cutting grass is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
to bat is to have an innings at cricket

explanation.surface: A small Australian trims the lawn before going out to bat at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a team's or batter's turn at the wicket in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing marsupial native to Australia, smallish and stocky.

clue.text: Uneasy feeling of some Asians, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: Malays are a people of south-east Asia

explanation.surface: Some Asian people are said to be feeling unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague sense of discomfort or unease is a general ill feeling.

clue.text: Immaculate round cigar

parts.note: immaculate means flawless, perfect
O, a round shape, is the letter

explanation.surface: Someone admires a flawless round cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cigar tapered at both ends is a recognised shape of cigar.

clue.text: Fortitude needed for our G imprisonment?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Fortitude needed for our G imprisonment?' — COURAGE is OUR inside CAGE, but the stray 'G' has no role and 'imprisonment' would be both CAGE and the insertion indicator; no search gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fortitude needed for our G imprisonment?

clue.text: Fight 18 with new leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the referenced answer is swapped for a different one

parts.note: the answer to 18 across, an Australian marsupial

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another answer, given a fresh head, makes a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new leader' replaces W, the first letter of WOMBAT (18 across), with C; the clue does not say which letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed fighting between forces is a battle or fight.

clue.text: I am sure I will live to spring

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned way of saying I'm certain
read literally: I shall exist in order to leap

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation means I'm certain, while literally it says I shall be leaping, as in bounding.

clue.text: Bet with Irish money

definitions.meaning: the former pound of the Republic of Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: A gamble or wager is a bet, and the old currency unit of Ireland before the euro was its pound.

clue.text: Goes downhill in the winter

parts.note: goes downhill sounds like declining, but here it means sliding down snowy slopes on runners

explanation.surface: Something declines when the cold weather arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding down snowy slopes on long runners is the winter sport of descending mountains.

clue.text: The Spanish take it with English cream

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spaniards help themselves to some English cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the select few.

clue.text: Criticism of reliable type sending back bill

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, solid person

indicators.note: sending back means the word for bill is turned to run the other way

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A dependable sort complains as they return a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick hurled in anger is a figure for a harsh critical remark.

clue.text: Totally unimportant condition of orbiting astronaut?

definitions.text: Totally unimportant condition of orbiting astronaut?

parts.words: Totally unimportant condition of orbiting astronaut?
parts.note: having no weight can mean being of no importance, and also the floating state in orbit

explanation.surface: Someone asks what state a spaceman is in, implying it matters little.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any weight means lacking influence, and also describes the free-fall state in zero gravity.
